events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present our summer group show Mixed Flock: 30 Years, marking the celebration of the gallery’s thirtieth anniversary. Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. Mixed Flock: 30 Years features work from represented and invited artists including: Anna Gray + Ryan Wilson Pauslen, Nick Blosser, Iván Carmona, Marjorie Dial, Amjad Faur, Bean Finneran, Jacques Flechemueller, Ellen George, Johannes GiararVictoria Haven, Elizabeth Knight, Justin L’Amie, Alma Allen, James Lavadour, Terran Last Gun, Nathan William Lambdin, Nancy Lorenz, Kristen Miller, Wes Mills, Jeffry Mitchell, Megan Murphy, Jenene Nagy, Ido Radon, Georgina Reskala, Joe Rudko, Tad Savinar, Susan Seubert, Adam Sorensen, Barbara Stafford, Storm Tharp, Gus Van Sant, Nell Warren, Heather Watkins, Marie Watt, and Yamamoto Masao.

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. In 2025, she was featured in Create! Magazine Issue #49 and is currently represented by Chefas Projects.
events.title: JESSIE WEITZEL LE GRAND | ASTRAL ACCESSORIES

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: In Allison Saft's enthralling new romantic fantasy, a chess grandmaster will go to any length to save the person she loves the most. Six years ago, Shea Fury's sister was whisked away by the High King of the Otherworld, the ruler of the treacherous land of fae. Although Shea has spent the years since dreaming of rescuing her sister from captivity, the Iron Veil that separates the human world from that of the fae has made it only a wish. That is, until an invitation to participate in a once-in-a-lifetime chess tournament in the Otherworld arrives on Shea's doorstep. The winner of the tournament may ask the High King to grant one wish, and Shea is finally within reach of hers. But entering the tournament and winning it are two different matters. Dark magic lurks around every corner in the Otherworld, and Shea's cutthroat opponents are willing to bend the rules to make their own wishes come true. To make it to the end — and to find her sister — she is forced to strike an alliance with her longtime rival, the sharply beautiful fae princess, Ciara of Bri Leith. One wrong move, though, and Shea could lose more than just the competition: she'd lose her sister, her dignity, and maybe even her life. In Immortal Game \(Wednesday Books\), Saft has written a high-stakes sapphic love story brimming with competitive tension set against a lush, Irish folklore-inspired fantasy world. Saft will be joined in conversation by Courtney Gould, author of What the Woods Took. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/allison-saft-9781250404763

events.summary: 21\+ Pickle your peter with the Forty Drop Few and Astral Projections, and come for an evening of old time music and early 1900s stag films projected on 16mm. The film selection, which comes from the Nyback Archive, includes some incredibly rare films that can’t be seen in any other way. As a collector of antique smut, I was thrilled to find out about Ioana and Garrett’s collection of early 1900s stag reels. This event is an absolute DELIGHT for me not only because I’m obsessed with antique porn, but also because I get to help choose which stag films were showing AND I get to play music for you all while we’re watching them. As soon as photography and videography were invented, they were used to make pornography. The making and distribution of pornographic materials was completely illegal due to the Comstock Act of 1873 and these obscenity restrictions were not relaxed until 1957. These laws of course did not slow down the production of porn by much, folks were just careful with their distribution. The films were mostly viewed at brothels and men’s stag parties. The majority of the women who acted and modeled for films and photos were sex workers who were found through brothels. I find antique pornography beautiful, interesting, educational, and a wonderful eye-opening connection between the past and the present. I am always showing it and have given a few presentations on it at PCC. People are too frequently shocked that it can be just a crazy as pornography today. They always say “they were doing that back then???” Of course they were! They were just as intense, just as freaky, just as weird, and also unfortunately just as evil as we are today. But we will only be showing the good stuff! So please join us for an evening of beautiful, freaky, weird, sexy, shocking old porn from the early 1900s! And also, wouldn’t it be great for Ioana and Garrett to be able to digitally transfer their entire collection of stag reels so that we can perhaps create an online archive of our very own? Do you have ideas for funding a project like that? Do you want to fund a project like that? If so please hit me up! Candle Sue 21 \+ only , I.D. will be checked at the door for admission.
events.title: Wonders of the Unseen World: A Night of Stag Films on 16mm

events.summary: Aquilon Music Festival invites you to an opera night at the historic Rossi Family Farms! This event will be catered by a great Italian-American chef Greg Demaestri! I Pagliacci (1892) is a seminal work of Italian realism. This gripping opera by Ruggero Leoncavallo (1857-1919) tells the story of a traveling troupe of actors whose lives mirror the drama they perform on stage. Canio, the leader of the troupe, becomes consumed by jealousy when he suspects his wife, Nedda, of being unfaithful. As tensions rise, personal betrayals spill into the evening’s comic performance. Forced to entertain the audience while his heart is breaking, Canio struggles to separate his role as a clown from his real emotions. The opera culminates in a shocking and tragic finale, where the boundary between theater and reality disappears completely. This is a piano-vocal production that employs an all-professional cast: Canio: Brennen Guillory, Tenor Nedda: Megan Belov, Soprano Tonio: Anton Belov, Baritone Silvio: Harry Baechtel, Baritone Anthony Nguyen, Tenor Stanislav Serebriannikov, Piano

This event is free as part of PAM's Free First Thursday , thanks to generous support provided by Art Bridges Foundation's Access for All program. THE EXPERIENCE Thursday, August 6th, 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of the horrific Hiroshima atomic bombing, an event which changed the course of humanity. Marking this occasion, local filmmaker David Paul-Heberg will premiere his new documentary The Seeds of Peace about a survivor of the bombing who continues to spread a message of peace by collecting seeds from trees that survived the blast and spreading them across the Pacific Northwest. A special post-film conversation will take place between David-Paul Hedberg, Dr. Vincent Intondi of Oregon Physicians for Social Responsibility, and Hanako Wakatsuki-Chong of the Japanese American Museum of Oregon. It will focus on the local connections to this story and how we can all continue to remember Hiroshima and Nagasaki today. Come early for a special performance by Oregon Koto-Kai . ON SCREEN: The Seeds of Peace 2026. Directed by David Paul-Hedberg. Runtime: 67 minutes. The Seeds of Peace traces the work of Hideko Tamura Snider, who survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima as a child. Decades later, she continues to spread the message of peaceby collecting seeds from trees that survived the blast and spreading them across the Pacific Northwest.This is a filmabout remembrance, reconciliation, and hope. It examines how the trauma of history can be transformed into a force that unites people and builds bridges for future generations. ON STAGE: Hanako Wakatuski-Chong \(Panelist\) - Hanako Wakatsuki-Chong is the executive director of the Japanese American Museum of Oregon in Portland. She has nearly two decades of experience working for state and federal agencies at the Idaho State Historical Society, the U.S. Navy, the National Park Service, and the White House Office of the Chief of Staff; holding roles as Interpretive Specialist, Education Specialist, Chief of Interpretation and Education, Superintendent, and Policy Advisor throughout her government career. In 2021, Wakatsuki-Chong received the Esto Perpetua Award for Lifetime Achievement from the Idaho State Historical Society for her work in preservation of Japanese American incarceration history in Idaho. She holds a BA in history and BS in political science from Boise State University, as well as an MA in museum studies from Johns Hopkins University, where she serves as an adjunct faculty member for their Krieger School of Arts and Sciences Museum Studies and Cultural Heritage Management Programs. Dr. Vincent Intondi \(Panelist\) - Dr. Vincent Intondi is the Executive Director of Oregon Physicians for Social Responsibility and a non-resident scholar at Cornell University's Reppy Institute for Peace and Conflict Studies. A nuclear disarmament expert whose research focuses on the intersection of race and nuclear weapons, from 2023-2024, Intondi was a senior lecturer in the International Relations department at Webster University-Leiden in the Netherlands. From 2013-2023, Intondi was a full-professor of history and founder and director of the Institute for Race, Justice, and Civic Engagement at Montgomery College in Takoma Park, Maryland. Prior to teaching at Montgomery College, Intondi served as director of research for American University's Nuclear Studies Institute in Washington, DC and was an associate professor of history at Seminole State College in Sanford, Florida. Intondi is the author of African Americans Against the Bomb: Nuclear Weapons, Colonialism, and the Black Freedom Movement \(Stanford University Press\) and Saving the World from Nuclear War: The June 12, 1982, Disarmament Rally and Beyond \(Johns Hopkins University Press\). David Paul-Hedberg \(Director\) - David-Paul \(Dave\) Hedberg is an independent historian and resident filmmaker at NW Documentary in Portland, Oregon. He has collaboratively produced historical exhibitions, films, and publications for clients across the Pacific Northwest. He brings his skills as an archival researcher and oral historian to filmmaking to help shine light on lesser known characters, historical topics, and places. His work is grounded in archival research, the shared authority of oral history and elder testimony, and a deep connection to the history and landscape of the Pacific Northwest. events.summary: When an auto dealership in Longview, TX, launches an endurance contest, ten economically strapped strangers embark on a journey that tests their hearts, minds, and bodies. events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Instrumental delivery can be a necessary medical intervention during childbirth, but when forceps or a vacuum extractor are used incorrectly, mothers may suffer serious physical and emotional harm. Injuries such as severe perineal tears, pelvic floor damage, nerve injuries, excessive bleeding, or long-term pain can have lasting effects on daily life. If these injuries resulted from avoidable medical errors or substandard care, the affected mother may have grounds to pursue a compensation claim. Establishing negligence typically requires evidence that healthcare professionals failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that this directly caused the injury. Every case is unique, so medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the delivery are carefully evaluated. Claims can help recover compensation for medical expenses, rehabilitation, lost income, ongoing care, and pain and suffering. The physical and emotional Traume from Instrumental Delivery may also be considered when assessing the full impact of the injury on the mother's quality of life. Understanding your legal rights is an important first step toward seeking justice. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance to individuals who believe their injuries were caused by negligent medical treatment. Their experience in investigating childbirth-related negligence helps clients understand whether they have a valid claim and what legal options may be available. Seeking legal advice promptly can also help preserve important evidence and ensure claims are brought within the applicable time limits.
events.title: Maternal injuries during instrumental delivery lead to compensation claims?

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. By combining detailed medical evidence with legal expertise, the firm helps clients understand their rights and pursue fair compensation where negligence has contributed to avoidable birth injuries.
events.title: How do medical experts assess injuries caused by assisted childbirth?

events.summary: When parents suspect that a birth injury could have been prevented, taking prompt and informed action is essential. The first step is to seek appropriate medical care for the child and ensure that all ongoing health concerns are properly documented. Parents should also request copies of medical records, including labour, delivery, and neonatal care notes, as these documents may help clarify what happened during childbirth. It is often beneficial to keep a detailed record of symptoms, treatments, and conversations with healthcare providers. In some situations, concerns may arise about Traume from Instrumental Delivery, particularly if forceps or a vacuum extractor were used during a difficult birth and the child later developed injuries. While not every complication is the result of negligence, a thorough legal review can determine whether accepted medical standards were followed. Understanding the cause of a birth injury can help families make informed decisions about their next steps. Experienced legal professionals can explain the claims process, the evidence required, and the applicable time limits without creating unnecessary stress for parents. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on medical negligence cases, including birth injury claims, and provides guidance to families seeking answers after a traumatic delivery. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters can help parents understand whether avoidable errors may have contributed to their child's injuries. events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases and understands the detailed approach required to investigate Surgical Negligence claims. Their experience in reviewing medical evidence and working with independent experts helps clients present well-supported claims. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.

events.summary: Camp overview Learn how to turn ideas into illustrated stories and investigate the connections between art books, comics, zines, and graphic novels in this weeklong camp for youth ages 11-14. Guided by teaching artist, ceramicist, and zine maker Erika Rier, campers will explore how images and words combine to tell powerful stories while developing their own unique illustration and storytelling styles. Throughout the week, campers will learn about the history and cultural impact of graphic novels and zines, examining how artists use these forms to share personal stories, ideas, and perspectives. Using traditional zinester tools like copiers, printers, staplers, and a variety of techniques including pop-up features and hand-cut pages, campers will experiment with layout, sequencing, and book construction as they create their own comics and zines. They’ll practice essential creative skills including narrative storytelling, character development, visual sequencing, and hand-drawn book design. Through collaborative activities and group discussions, they’ll share ideas, give feedback, and turn everyday moments into imaginative, original comics and zines. On the last day of camp, participants will showcase their work in an exhibition for family and friends. This camp offers youth the power to grow confidence in their creative voice and a deeper understanding of the power of visual storytelling. register for panels to pages About the teaching artist Erika Rier is a self-taught interdisciplinary artist creating mostly ceramics and art zines in a style she calls folk surrealism. Writing was her first love and she still secretly writes stories. Having lived in Maine, Vermont, Connecticut, NYC, Arizona, and Washington state; Erika now resides in Portland, OR. She also has one of each of the following: a husband, a daughter, and a cat she found in a hallway.

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present our summer group show Mixed Flock: 30 Years, marking the celebration of the gallery’s thirtieth anniversary. Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. Mixed Flock: 30 Years features work from represented and invited artists including: Anna Gray + Ryan Wilson Pauslen, Nick Blosser, Iván Carmona, Marjorie Dial, Amjad Faur, Bean Finneran, Jacques Flechemueller, Ellen George, Johannes GiararVictoria Haven, Elizabeth Knight, Justin L’Amie, Alma Allen, James Lavadour, Terran Last Gun, Nathan William Lambdin, Nancy Lorenz, Kristen Miller, Wes Mills, Jeffry Mitchell, Megan Murphy, Jenene Nagy, Ido Radon, Georgina Reskala, Joe Rudko, Tad Savinar, Susan Seubert, Adam Sorensen, Barbara Stafford, Storm Tharp, Gus Van Sant, Nell Warren, Heather Watkins, Marie Watt, and Yamamoto Masao.

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. In 2025, she was featured in Create! Magazine Issue #49 and is currently represented by Chefas Projects.

events.summary: This summer, a multi-sensory art experience called Shifting Realities will take over Porsche Studio Portland for a creative journey produced by artists from Portland and across the country. The space turns into a living canvas where you don’t just observe the work, you become part of it. Across multiple interactive environments, you’ll see sound take physical form, design in real time using light and gesture, and step into spaces that respond to your movement, energy, and input. From large-scale visual installations to hands-on creative moments and a multisensory tasting experience, each part of the experience is designed to blur the line between artist and audience. Guests move through the experience in timed groups, progressing together through each space while still having room to explore and interact along the way. Running June 4 through August 31, Shifting Realities is a 100 minute limited-run installation that’s built for all ages and occasions. Tickets start at $39 ($41.34 incl. fees), with reduced pricing for kids and options for VIP, private, and group bookings.

events.summary: Join us at ADX on August 7th for the opening night of Elementals by Lindsay Spina, Cynthia Veum, and Rick Shearing. The show will be accompanied by a music showcase by Ezra Meredith and the Deer Lodge All Stars, and a small bar. August 7th, 5-9 PM. 417 SE 11th Avenue. Free Event. Elementals celebrates the beauty, resilience, and transformative power of the natural world through painting, natural materials, and ceramics. Featuring the work of local art therapists Lindsay Spina and Cynthia Veum, alongside high school art teacher Rick Shearing, the exhibition brings together three distinct artistic voices united by a shared reverence for nature as both inspiration and teacher. Drawing from organic forms, landscapes, and the elemental forces that shape our environment, each artist explores the ways in which creativity fosters growth, healing, and connection. Through expressive painting, tactile ceramic forms, and works incorporating natural materials, the exhibition reflects on cycles of change, renewal, and the profound relationship between humans and the world around them. As practicing art therapists, Spina and Veum approach their work with an understanding of art as a vehicle for reflection, emotional exploration, and restoration, while Shearing's perspective as an educator highlights the enduring role of creative practice in cultivating curiosity and self-expression. Together, their work invites viewers to slow down, engage their senses, and consider the elemental forces that shape both the landscapes we inhabit and our own inner lives. Elementals offers a contemplative space where art becomes a bridge between the external environment and personal experience, encouraging visitors to reflect on transformation, resilience, and the enduring connections that bind us to the natural world.

events.summary: Get lost in color at Los Hongos! Paint a frog & mushroom with artist guidance, great bevs, and room for experimentation :) Come spend an evening getting lost in color at Los Hongos Cafe & Plant Bar! I’m Kate, a Portland -based artist and member of visionary art collective The Haven PDX. My work is rooted in bold color, symbolism, and the creation of strange energetic worlds. For this community paint night, we’ll all begin with an original design: a frog perched on a mushroom beneath a moonlight sky. Where you go with it is completely up to you. I’ll provide guidance, demonstrate different techniques, and help you along the way, but there’s no single version of the painting we’re all trying to recreate. Use whatever colors you’re drawn to. Try a technique you’ve never used before. Follow my painting closely, change a few things, or take the whole thing somewhere completely different. Regardless, i'm excited to see what you cook up! No painting experience is necessary. This is a chance to spend a few hours absorbed in color, try something new, meet some people, and make something with your own two hands. We’ll be painting at Los Hongos, a mushroom-centric café and gathering space in SE Portland. Note: Los Hongos does not serve alcohol, but they offer a range of adaptogenic and functional beverages alongside a full coffee menu. Food will also be available for purchase throughout the evening. Come alone, bring a friend, or make it a date <3 All painting materials are included, and you’ll leave with a finished piece that is completely your own :) I'll see you there!

THE EXPERIENCE Join us for an activation by Skate Like a Girl before a screening of Skate Dreams: the first feature documentary about the rise of women's skateboarding. ON SCREEN: Skate Dreams 2022. Directed by Jessica Edwards. Runtime: 1 hour 22 minutes. Skate Dreams, the first feature documentary about the rise of women's skateboarding, profiles a group of women whose pursuit of self-expression, equality, and freedom have created an international movement on and off their skateboards. From their boycott of the X-Games, to their defiance of traditional skateboarding gatekeepers, through grueling worldwide skate competitions in the run up to the Olympics, Skate Dreams showcases the charismatic personalities, indomitable spirits and amazing talent of these trailblazing pioneers. HOSTED BY: Skate Like A Girl For 25 years, Skate Like a Girl has been building community, breaking barriers, and making skateboarding more inclusive. It all started in 2000 when Fleur Larsen, Holly Sheehan, and a passionate crew of volunteers began hosting clinics, camps, and contests in Olympia, Washington. With our move to Seattle in 2005 and the leadership of Nancy Chang, we became an official 501\(c\)\(3\) nonprofit, setting the stage for even greater impact. Soon after, new chapters took root in Portland, thanks to Benji Haungs, and in the SF Bay Area, led by Erica Harris. In 2009, Wheels of Fortune was launched alongside our Youth Employment Skateboarding \(YES\) teen leadership program. Wheels of Fortune 7 was an X-Games qualifier in 2016-bringing the event to the global stage, showing how we continue to push boundaries. We've reimagined programs to better reflect our values, like our Women and/or Trans Sessions, creating space for skaters of all identities. Through challenges like the 2020 pandemic, we've adapted stayed and connected, offering virtual programs and learn-to-skate resources, as well as launching initiatives like the Skateboarding Inclusivity Cooperative \(S.I.C.\) and Overnight Camp in the Sequoias. Today, we reach over 12,000 participants annually across Seattle, Portland, and the Bay Area with programs for all ages, abilities, and identities. events.summary: When the Dashwood sisters lose their fortune and home due to inheritance laws that favor male heirs, sensible Elinor and romantic Marianne must navigate a new life of reduced circumstances—and matters of the heart. Elinor quietly bears her heartbreak over Edward Ferrars, while Marianne passionately pursues the dashing but unreliable Willoughby. As secrets unravel and true characters reveal themselves, the sisters discover that finding love requires both sense and sensibility. Jane Austen's timeless story explores themes that resonate as strongly today as they did in Regency England: the tension between following your head and following your heart, the economic vulnerabilities women face, the importance of integrity over charm, and the resilience required to rebuild your life when circumstances change. Through sharp wit and keen observation of human nature, Austen reminds us that neither pure rationality nor unchecked emotion alone can navigate life's complexities—we need both. Roger Parsley and Andy Graham have streamlined Austen's beloved novel into a fast-moving adaptation that retains all the delicate irony, spirit, and romance of the original. Their version brings these universal themes to vivid life, proving that questions about authenticity, financial security, and the courage to be vulnerable in love are as relevant in the 21st century as they were 200 years ago. Join us for an enchanting summer evening amid the hazelnut trees as we celebrate the enduring power of Austen's insight into the human heart.
events.title: Sense and Sensibility

events.summary: Opera at the scenic Lady Hill Winery! I Pagliacci (1892) is a seminal work of Italian realism. Canio, the leader of the troupe, becomes consumed by jealousy when he suspects his wife, Nedda, of being unfaithful. As tensions rise, personal betrayals spill into the evening’s comic performance. Forced to entertain the audience while his heart is breaking, Canio struggles to separate his role as a clown from his real emotions. The opera culminates in a shocking and tragic finale, where the boundary between theater and reality disappears completely. This is a piano-vocal production that employs an all-professional cast. events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/Cray26 On Sale Friday, May 8th at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Blues icon. Soul man. Rock and roller. Robert Cray is all these things – and more. The Georgiaborn, Washington-raised musician first picked up a guitar after seeing The Beatles on TV then, having witnessed Jimi Hendrix perform in Seattle, determined that his destiny would also follow a similar path. And so he has: across the past half century Robert Cray’s developed into one of American music’s most singular artists. "I guess you'd have to say that we were lucky,” reflects Cray on his life in music, “because, growing up in the 1960s, the different music played on the radio really opened us up. I mean, we even had Albert Collins play our high School graduation party." From forming a teenage garage band, through to striding the stage alongside several of the world’s greatest guitarists, Robert Cray’s story is one of struggle and commitment. Struggle and commitment that led to Cray enjoying phenomenal success – selling millions of albums and countless concert tickets, winning five Grammy Awards, being inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame, recipient of the Americana Music Lifetime Achievement Award, designing two signature model Fender guitars – yet for Robert what’s always mattered most is the music. Every note he plays counts, every song he sings is delivered as if it is his last: integrity and intensity are what has guided Cray’s musical career. He has never cheapened his output or delivered a substandard performance. Indeed, his commitment to making music of the highest standard has won Cray both a loyal audience and the respect of many of popular music’s most legendary figures. Think about it: Robert Cray has shared stage and/or studio with the likes of John Lee Hooker, Muddy Waters, B.B. King, Buddy Guy, Chuck Berry, Albert Collins, The Rolling Stones, Eric Clapton, Tina Turner, Stevie Ray Vaughan, the Memphis Horns and Hi Rhythm Section. Cray’s stinging guitar playing and soulful voice, his skills as a band leader and performer, mark him as keeper of the flame for American roots music, an artist who never fails to deliver. "We were so lucky just be able to see them,” says Cray of trading guitar licks on stage with legends of blues, rock and soul, “let alone share the stage with them - what an experience!"
events.title: The Robert Cray Band

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. By combining detailed medical evidence with legal expertise, the firm helps clients understand their rights and pursue fair compensation where negligence has contributed to avoidable birth injuries.

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.

Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present our summer group show Mixed Flock: 30 Years, marking the celebration of the gallery’s thirtieth anniversary. Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. Mixed Flock: 30 Years features work from represented and invited artists including: Anna Gray + Ryan Wilson Pauslen, Nick Blosser, Iván Carmona, Marjorie Dial, Amjad Faur, Bean Finneran, Jacques Flechemueller, Ellen George, Johannes GiararVictoria Haven, Elizabeth Knight, Justin L’Amie, Alma Allen, James Lavadour, Terran Last Gun, Nathan William Lambdin, Nancy Lorenz, Kristen Miller, Wes Mills, Jeffry Mitchell, Megan Murphy, Jenene Nagy, Ido Radon, Georgina Reskala, Joe Rudko, Tad Savinar, Susan Seubert, Adam Sorensen, Barbara Stafford, Storm Tharp, Gus Van Sant, Nell Warren, Heather Watkins, Marie Watt, and Yamamoto Masao.

Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. In 2025, she was featured in Create! Magazine Issue #49 and is currently represented by Chefas Projects.
events.title: JESSIE WEITZEL LE GRAND | ASTRAL ACCESSORIES

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: Farewell brings the inaugural Classical Northwest festival to a poignant and elegant close. Framed by music of parting and reflection, the program pairs Mozart’s Concerto for Three Pianos with Haydn’s Farewell Symphony. Together, these works offer grace, wit, and gentle introspection, ending the festival not with spectacle, but with warmth, humanity, and a memorable goodbye. The Classical Northwest is a new, community‑centered classical music festival debuting this August in the Portland area. Founded on the belief that great music thrives through collaboration and shared experience, the festival brings together more than 60 musicians spanning generations and backgrounds—youth ensembles, community orchestras, and some of the region’s most respected professional artists—performing side by side in a unique celebration of classical music. In proud partnership with organizations such as Fear No Music, All Classical Radio, and the Metropolitan Youth Symphony, The Classical Northwest highlights the richness of the region’s musical ecosystem while fostering mentorship, artistic exchange, and access to live classical performance. Through orchestral and chamber concerts that honor tradition while embracing community, the festival aims to create an inclusive space where musicians and audiences alike can connect through timeless music.
events.title: The Classical Northwest presents: Farewell

events.summary: When an auto dealership in Longview, TX, launches an endurance contest, ten economically strapped strangers embark on a journey that tests their hearts, minds, and bodies. The contestant who keeps at least one hand on a brand-new hardbody truck the longest gets to drive it off the lot. What initially seems like a mere publicity stunt soon becomes a soul-baring battle of wills. Only one can win, but for all involved, the truck holds the key to their own private American dream. The mix of people in this contest includes: an unlikeable prior winner who is a bit racist; the son of an immigrant who wants to be a veterinarian; a USMC veteran; an older woman (with her husband for support) who really needs the money; a Texas evangelical; a beauty queen; an older man (and his wife as support) who is recovering from a fall from a big rig; and a few other folks. The backstory involves the faltering dealership, lack of sales, and unethical behavior by some of the staff.

events.summary: Shakespeare in the park? How about Shakespeare in the library; Shakespeare in the dive bar; Shakespeare in the strip club! Contender for most Portland thing ever? For our 11th season, join Speculative Drama for a festival of pop-up Shakespeare with Bard Bites!, bringing theatre to all the places that make our city unique and special. This three weekend series consists of our signature Speculations: free, incredibly queer and immersive pop-up Shakespeare scenes; and culminates in a world-premier workshop production of A Walking Shadow: an all-new one hour fringe production inspired by Shakespeare’s most infamous queen, Lady Macbeth. PLUS! Don’t miss our special double-feature on Friday, July 31st - a showing of A Walking Shadow followed by a bite-sized production of Portland’s own literary burlesque show Booklover’s Burlesque at the Victoria Belle! What To Expect: Bard Bites! kicks off with a series of 100% FREE Shakespeare pop-ups, all leading up to a Pay-What-You-Are-Able world premier workshop production of A Walking Shadow. The festival includes a ticketed double-feature evening of Shakespeare, burlesque, and blood with Booklover’s Burlesque: Shakespeare Edition and A Walking Shadow on Friday, July 31st. Event Schedule: 7/25 - Speculations - Skidmore Fountain, Kit Kat Club - Times and scene list available at rsvpdx.com/bardbites 7/26 - Speculations - Angelo’s Bar, Hawthorne Plaza - Times and scene list available at rsvpdx.com/bardbites 7/31 - bite-sized *Booklover’s Burlesque: Shakespeare Edition* and *A Walking Shadow* double-feature - The Victorian Belle 1441 N McClellan St - 8pm, 7pm door 8/01 - Speculations - Central Library, Director Park - Times and scene list available at rsvpdx.com/bardbites 8/08 - *Speculations -* Angelo’s Bar, Hawthorne Plaza - Times and scene list available at rsvpdx.com/bardbites 8/09 - *A Walking Shadow* workshop production - Back Door Theater 4319 SE Hawthorne Blvd - 6pm & 8pm Speculative Drama is a program under Misfit Academy, a performance oriented 501(c)3 and all donations are tax-deductible. A note on accessibility: These performances are immersive, roaming performances in various indoor and outdoor spaces. All venues are ADA accessible. Masks are highly encouraged for audience members. Performers will move throughout the venues, and audience members should be prepared to be within 6 foot proximity of unmasked performers and other audience members. Please email us at speculative.drama@gmail.com with any accommodation questions or concerns. Directors: Myrrh Larsen\, David Berkson *Speculations Performers: Myrrh Larsen*, Megan Skye Hale*, Anna Nymph, Biz Bellows, Damian Luis, Darius Haas, Isaac Ellingson, Isabella Buckner, J.J. Hawkins, Katie Mortemore, Lauren Trask, Meg Morrigan, Megan Haynes, Phoenix Cox, Wendy Wilcox **A Walking Shadow Written and Devised by: Megan Skye Hale and Myrrh Larsen Booklover’s Burlesque Created and Produced by: Lacy Knightly Speculative Drama Artistic Director: Megan Skye Hale\, *Creative and Technical Director:* Myrrh Larsen\ \indicates Speculative Drama company member *About Speculative Drama:* Speculative Drama aims to reclaim the relevance of myths, fairy tales, and classical texts through immersive, live theatrical performances. Our goal is to better reflect the diversity of the communities which we serve, and to show fellow people of marginalized identities that we, too, have a place in the classics. Through site-specific theatre, rich and immersive soundscapes, and an extremely intimate setting we explore the intersection of classic stories and unconventional storytelling - creating an atmosphere of inclusion and innovation while honoring and maintaining the original texts or source materials. *Praise for past Speculative Drama Shakespeare productions:* “As masterful as the Bard was, in this case, it’s the contemporary artists, with their verve and vision, who hold us in awe…In this environment… iambic pentameter sounds as natural as water rippling over rocks.” — Linda Ferguson, Willamette Week on Twelfth Night https://www.wweek.com/arts/theater/2024/01/09/speculative-drama-performs-william-shakespeares-twelfth-night-at-local-dive-bar-angelos/ “Having the play \[Twelfth Night\] unfold next to me, instead of on a stage, made it feel so much more real. For one, the actors were closer and easier to see. But even more: the cast did such a good job that, at moments, my brain truly forgot they weren't just fellow humans hanging out at the bar.” — Darryl Micaud, audience member. “\[Speculative Drama\] consistently produces immersive shows that make you think about old stories in new ways; that's what makes them one of the most exciting and innovative theatre companies in the Pacific Northwest.” — Dr. Jess Hebert, audience member *Photo Credits**: Promotional design by Myrrh Larsen, juice box and apple illustration by Therese Arturo.
