events.summary: Carolyn Wonderland, with her dynamic guitar playing, formidable songwriting, and pure Texas vocals, has more than earned her reputation as a fiercely independent artist. Wonderland plays original, bluesified, cosmic soul music, mixed with heavy doses of Tex-Mex and riff-fueled rock 'n' roll. She has been performing professionally since the age of 15 and has led a colorful and adventurous life. On the road her entire career, she's played with icons from Townes Van Zandt to Levon Helm, from Buddy Guy to Hubert Sumlin, from Bob Dylan to John Mayall, all while writing her own story. On her new Alligator Records album, Truth Is, Wonderland, with her vividly detailed, instantly memorable songs, reflects on the world with honesty and righteous conviction. Wonderland's bold and insightful songs tell common-sense truths that, in her words, "need to be told." They are driven by her sometimes savage and other times gently melodic guitar fingerpicking, along with her full-throated yet still vulnerable vocals. As for the album's brutally honest subject matter, Wonderland says, "There's always hope and we're still here for each other, but at some point, you have to sing about the elephant in the room." With Truth Is, Carolyn Wonderland stakes her claim among the most influential roots music voices today, delivering the blues' honest truth to all who will listen. Her courageously empowering music packs an emotional wallop, with every track on the album performed with a rare intensity that is welcoming and ultimately uplifting. "She's something else," Bob Dylan once said to Ray Benson. "She should be nationwide." Minors ok with parent/guardian Review our venue FAQ here ALL SALES ARE FINAL. PLEASE, DOUBLE CHECK YOUR ORDER BEFORE PURCHASING. NO REFUNDS.
events.title: Carolyn Wonderland with special guest Kelly's Lot

events.summary: The Literary Arts Bookstore & Cafe is pleased to welcome author Kelly Anderson to celebrate the release of book, The Wild Beneath. Anderson will be joined in conversation by Rachel Hochhauser. About the book: For readers of Wild Dark Shore and The Time Traveler’s Wife, a fierce, haunting story of one woman caught between her first love and a mysterious stranger who upends everything—and the two worlds that won’t let her go. Annie MacLeod always knew she was different, growing up on a sailboat in the Pacific Northwest, navigating by stars and swimming with sea creatures alongside her parents and best friend Evan. But when a tsunami shatters her world, Annie is stranded on land and forced to confront how eccentric she is. In the wreckage, she rescues a wordless man named Walker, who emits a hum only she can hear. Their connection is instant, electric. Walker’s touch gives Annie visions of the ocean’s hidden world, a life she’s never known but feels inexplicably drawn to. Yet even as she is pulled toward him, Evan—the steadfast love who has always been there—remains on dry land, offering the stability she may have to leave behind. Annie is torn between Evan’s grounding presence and Walker’s magnetic secrets. But then, Walker vanishes, along with the answers she needs about who she really is. Six years later, Annie has left the sea and buried the past—until Walker’s otherworldly sound returns, pulling her back toward the ocean and the life she abandoned. The truth under the water is more ancient than she ever could have known, and Annie must confront a choice that will test her heart and determine her future.
events.title: Kelly Anderson in conversation with Rachel Hochhauser

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/CBR26 On Sale Now! This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- “Three little birds sat on my window.. .. And they told me I don't need to worry” And so began the song that would change then-25-year-old Corinne Bailey Rae’s life. Now on over a billion streams, Put Your Records On, and the US and UK number one self-titled debut album that followed, propelled her from jazz club hostess to a platinum-selling artist. Bailey Rae would go on to win two Grammy Awards \(plus a further four nominations\), two MOBOS, two Mercury Music Prize nominations and a BET Award. The world fell hard for Bailey Rae’s jazzinflected soul stylings, while in the UK she became the fourth female act in history to have her first album debut at number one in the US, selling over four million copies in the process. That indelible opening lyric was a playful nod to Bob Marley & The Wailers’ Three Little Birds, and to celebrate the 20th anniversary of her breakout hit in 2026, both songs will find a new and unexpected audience via Bailey Rae’s latest project: a children's book. Beautifully illustrated by Gillian Eilidh O'Mara, Put Your Records On follows a young protagonist, Bea, discovering her great aunt's record collection. It’s a celebration of music’s therapeutic power and intergenerational bonds. “Would you like to hear a song that feels like sunshine?” asks Aunt Portia, before playing Bea Bob Marley’s Three Little Birds. ‘Music can take you on such a journey and help you understand your emotions,’ says Bailey Rae. ‘I have young children and I love the idea of a child discovering a collection of music like a secret garden. That you could open these doors and find so much art and so much feeling inside.’ Bailey Rae’s love of records reaches back to childhood, where her own collection spanned Nirvana, Jimi Hendrix and Mariah Carey. It’s fitting that, to celebrate Record Store Day in Spring 2026, she will release a reissue of 2007’s Live in New York album. Recorded at New York’s iconic Webster Hall, it features orchestral-backed versions of her chart-topping hits including Call Me When You Get This, Trouble Sleeping and Put Your Records On. ‘It felt like flying,’ she says of the shows. ‘Ever since being a teenager in a band, I get into a kind of flow onstage. It's transcendent.’ Bailey Rae will headline London’s famed Royal Albert Hall as a culmination of her 20 years Celebration throughout 2026.
events.title: Like a Star: Celebrating 20 Years of Corinne Bailey Rae

Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. events.summary: The Literary Arts Bookstore & Cafe is pleased to welcome author heidi restrepo rhodes to celebrate her debut short story collection, Ampersand Organ. About the book: A fearless, expansive collection that blurs the boundary between body and poem, wielding a liberatory lyric impulse that revels from neuron to nebula and back. Here is a book of many hearts, a revolutionary tide pool, a mycelial space and sensorium where our neural pathways are “always shared, collective, and entangled.” In this “more-than-human lyric,” heidi andrea restrepo rhodes offers the ampersand, a mode of encounter that unfixes the reader. This form—a lyric prose poem beginning, midsentence, with an ampersand—accesses the intimacies of a life shaped by perpetual “and-ing.” These ampersands move by associative leap, synesthetic braid, and inter-species blur to revel in everything that makes us more than singular subjects. Neuroqueering poetics, rhodes writes toward deft and loving excess: spillage, echolalia, stutter, loop, and non-linear detour, refiguring what the lyric can be and what the body can do. These poems revolt against all forms of supremacy, inviting us into unexpected kinship with animal, mineral, vegetal, and heavenly bodies, each replete with its own languages, temporalities, histories, and worlds. Tending an everyday eroticism with its “heart at the sleeve, in the palm,” Ampersand Organ is unafraid to feel, to feel again, to feel feeling wherever it’s wildly felt. Here is a radiant, divergent, emergent field guide for how we might all shiver and shimmer into the and and and . . .
events.title: heidi restrepo rhodes: Ampersand Organ

events.summary: Experience a world of magic at the Victorian Belle Mansion! This summer, two world class magicians share their timeless history of mystery from lands far and near. Join Professor Palshikar, a New York-based, second generation Indian magician as he visits the region and Portland-based Historical Conjurer, Professor DR Schreiber for an unique evening of mystery and history. WORLD OF MAGIC: From Conjurer to Jadugar Thursday, August 13th, 2026 Doors open at 7pm Show at 8pm The Victorian Belle Mansion 1441 N. McClellan Street Portland, OR ADVANCED TICKETS: VIP Front Row Table Single Seat - $40.00 Second Row Table Single Seat - $35.00 Tall Bistro Table for 4 People - $140.00 General Admission Single Ticket - $25.00 Standing Room Ticket - $20.00 Ticket prices are for the show only and do not include food/drink. All food and drink items may be purchased separately from The Belle's dinner menu. Door tickets increase by $10 each and are sold only if available on a first-come, first-served. Tickets at: https://victorianbelle.com/shows-events/ About the performers: Professor Palshikar Shreeyash is the leading performer of world magic. Born in India thirteen days after Halloween, his ancestors include a Mormon prophet, Hindu priest, and an Indian magician. He has lived and worked around the world for decades, and is now based in New York. He began performing in school, and has traveled the world ever since. Combining the best of East & West, Shreeyash created fusion jadoo. Executives, college presidents, city mayors, and even royalty enjoy his fun, unique, bespoke performances and talks. Dr. Palshikar earned a PhD in South Asian studies from University of Chicago and has taught at Oxford, Yale, the School of Oriental and African Studies in London, and Fordham University in New York. He won a Fulbright fellowship to study traditional Indian magic with the last living performers, and has studied Chicago magic and improv. He has collaborated with the American Centers in Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata, an Emmy award winning Broadway producer/director, New York based Bindlestiff Cirkus, the Asian Arts Initiative, WHYY, FirstPerson Arts, FringeArts, and others to share the wonder of Indian magic in venues around the world for 3 decades. He consulted on the Disney+ and Discovery series Beyond Belief, on a Vanishing Inc documentary, and is creating an original film on Indian magic. He has appeared on the Holland America World Cruises, at Harvard, Yale, and at the Smithsonian. Enjoy his fusion jadoo live, up close and in person: fun, enchanting, and enlightening. Audiences never forget it. Come, let him take a peek into your mind. Professor DR Schreiber The World of the Historical Conjurer Early in the 18th century, magic (or conjuring as it was referred) emerged as a genuine art form and entertainment. Professors of natural philosophy and conjuring would rent taverns, legitimate theaters or lecture halls for the exhibition and displays of legerdemain, necromancy, or what would today be called “illusion” and “magic tricks.” Top dollar would be paid by the citizens of Europe to see the latest discoveries in the science of “natural philosophy.” Today, Professor DR Schreiber presents an historic look at the beginnings of modern magic in his performances and exhibitions. Join Professor DR Schreiber as he leads you on a stroll through the past centuries of conjuring entertainment. His unique presentations entertain while educating the audience about historical events, literary and cultural figures, and the science and art of conjuring. Now you too can experience magic, as it was centuries ago. \------
events.title: WORLD OF MAGIC: From Conjurer to Jadugar

events.summary: From the writer Elle calls the "most inspiringly wicked social critic of the moment" comes a hands-on, don't-lose-hope study of how writers, painters, musicians, and other cultural figures respond to fascism. From veteran writer and activist Curtis White comes a concise yet potent guide to standing up to the myriad tyrannies of our current political landscape. We live in a time where independent thinking, love of literature and ideas, and passion for human expression are all under attack from a ruthless and uncaring government and a culture that values only immediate gratification and digital flash. In On Resistance \(Melville House\), White offers spiritual hope and intellectual fortification for those in despair about the bankruptcy of American life. Drawing on a range of books, films, essays, and artworks, White shows how our rich collective literary heritage gives us mental ammunition for our fight against the forces that would reduce us all to commodities and consumers. THE EXPERIENCE The state of Oregon is a magical place full of beautiful, diverse landscapes ranging from rugged ocean coastlines to rain-soaked temperate forests, arid high deserts and plains, fertile valleys, and volcanic mountain ranges, to name a few. Tonight we celebrate this majestic beauty by screening the 2014 film Wild, which was largely filmed in Oregon using the state's landscapes as stand-ins for other states' locations along the Pacific Coast Trail. Join us for a very special discussion with author Cheryl Strayed, whose memoir Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Crest Trail inspired the feature film Wild; William L. Sullivan, author of 28 books and guides and hundreds of articles about the Pacific Northwest; and filmmaker Ime Etuk, whose feature Outdoor School follows a young urban teenager discovering peace and comfort in the natural splendor we call Oregon. This program is made possible with a grant from the America 250 Oregon Commission. Following the conversation, we will screen the film Wild, based on the 2012 memoir by Cheryl Strayed. ON SCREEN: Wild 2014. Directed by Jean-Marc Vallée. Runtime: 115 minutes. Rated R. Based on the 2012 memoir by Cheryl Strayed Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Coast Trail, Wild follows a woman with a tragic past who decides to start her new life by hiking for one thousand miles on the Pacific Crest Trail. Filmed largely in Oregon. ON STAGE: Cheryl Strayed \(Author\) - Cheryl Strayed is the author of the \#1 New York Times bestseller Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Crest Trail, which was made into an Oscar-nominated film. Her bestselling collection of Dear Sugar columns, Tiny Beautiful Things, was adapted for a Hulu television show and as a play that continues to be staged in theaters nationwide. Strayed's other books are the critically acclaimed novel, Torch, and the bestselling collection Brave Enough, which brings together more than one hundred of her inspiring quotes. Her books have sold more than 5 million copies around the world and have been translated into forty languages. Her award-winning essays and short stories have been published in The Best American Essays, the New York Times, the Washington Post Magazine, Vogue, and elsewhere. Strayed is also a popular podcaster, having hosted the shows Sugar Calling and Dear Sugars, which she made with Steve Almond for the New York Times. She's now the host of the weekly podcast Mind Over Mountain for the iHeart Women's Sports network. She lives in Portland, Oregon. Photo credit Brian McDonnell. William L. Sullivan \(Author\) - William L. Sullivan is the author of 28 books and hundreds of articles about Oregon, including a weekly "Oregon Trails" column for Lookout: Eugene-Springfield . A fifth-generation Oregonian, Sullivan began hiking at the age of five and has been exploring new trails ever since. After studying at Deep Springs College in the California desert, receiving an English degree from Cornell University, and studying linguistics at Germany's Heidelberg University, he earned an M.A. in German literature from the University of Oregon. He has been happily married to the artist Janell Sorensen for more than 50 years. Sullivan's hobbies include backcountry ski touring, playing the pipe organ and harpsichord, reading foreign language novels, and promoting libraries. He co-chaired the campaign to build Eugene's downtown library, served on the Oregon State Library Board, and is president of the Lane Library League, a citizen group with the goal of extending library service to the 80,000 people in Lane County who currently lack service. Sullivan served for eight years on the board of the conservation group Oregon Wild and is a past president of the Round Table Club of Eugene. Sullivan organizes three author events each year-the Oregon Authors Table at the Art & the Vineyard Festival in Eugene on the 4th of July weekend, the Oregon Authors Table at the Oregon State Fair from late August through early September in Salem, and the Authors & Artists Fair, a fundraiser for the Lane Library League. Ime Etuk \(Filmmaker\) - Etuk believes the first step in storytelling is listening-deeply, openly, and without assumption. Whether writing, directing, or producing, he begins with rooting work in real stories and lived experiences. He aims to explore important emotional truths through fiction. His commitment is to honor communities and bring visibility to what's often overlooked or unheard. As a first-generation Nigerian raised in Portland, Etuk spent his life moving between cultural worlds-often translating himself in spaces that didn't fully see him. That sense of in-between shaped how he views identity, belonging, and transformation. It also drives the kinds of stories he tells: ones grounded in resilience, tension, and the quiet power of becoming. He is inspired by oral traditions, community histories, and the collective memory of those whose stories have too often been erased or ignored. His work draws on these influences and fuses them with his training in journalism, film, and theater. Over time, his practice has evolved from simply directing films to creating spaces for others to share their stories. He leads Lion Speaks, a nonprofit that mentors historically excluded Black and BIPOC creatives in media. Collaboration, mentorship, and access are central to his creative process. He often begins new work by listening: conducting interviews and gathering narratives that can be transformed into film, theater, or multimedia pieces. His goal is to build a body of work that is emotionally grounded and culturally expansive-films, series, and collaborative projects that foster reflection, empathy, and connection, while widening the circle of who gets to be seen and heard. His latest feature film, Outdoor School, premiered at the American Black Film Festival in 2025 and is currently on the festival circuit. Based on a true story, first shared on The Moth, and featured in the New York Times bestselling book, How to Tell a Story, the film explores themes of resilience, homelessness, and transformation in 1990's Portland.

Speaking with guests such as Lesley Woods of Au Pairs, Hugo Burnham of Gang Of Four, Stan Ridgway of Wall Of Voodoo & Steve Bartek of Oingo Boingo, they have gotten the history of this film and its artists firsthand. events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: When parents suspect that a birth injury could have been prevented, taking prompt and informed action is essential. The first step is to seek appropriate medical care for the child and ensure that all ongoing health concerns are properly documented. Parents should also request copies of medical records, including labour, delivery, and neonatal care notes, as these documents may help clarify what happened during childbirth. It is often beneficial to keep a detailed record of symptoms, treatments, and conversations with healthcare providers. In some situations, concerns may arise about Traume from Instrumental Delivery, particularly if forceps or a vacuum extractor were used during a difficult birth and the child later developed injuries. While not every complication is the result of negligence, a thorough legal review can determine whether accepted medical standards were followed. Understanding the cause of a birth injury can help families make informed decisions about their next steps. Experienced legal professionals can explain the claims process, the evidence required, and the applicable time limits without creating unnecessary stress for parents. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on medical negligence cases, including birth injury claims, and provides guidance to families seeking answers after a traumatic delivery. Most importantly, parents should remember that seeking legal advice is not only about pursuing compensation but also about obtaining accountability and securing support for their child's future care and long-term needs.

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases and understands the detailed approach required to investigate Surgical Negligence claims. Their experience in reviewing medical evidence and working with independent experts helps clients present well-supported claims. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.

events.summary: Instrumental delivery can be a necessary medical intervention during childbirth, but when forceps or a vacuum extractor are used incorrectly, mothers may suffer serious physical and emotional harm. If these injuries resulted from avoidable medical errors or substandard care, the affected mother may have grounds to pursue a compensation claim. events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present our summer group show Mixed Flock: 30 Years, marking the celebration of the gallery’s thirtieth anniversary. Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. Mixed Flock: 30 Years features work from represented and invited artists including: Anna Gray + Ryan Wilson Pauslen, Nick Blosser, Iván Carmona, Marjorie Dial, Amjad Faur, Bean Finneran, Jacques Flechemueller, Ellen George, Johannes GiararVictoria Haven, Elizabeth Knight, Justin L’Amie, Alma Allen, James Lavadour, Terran Last Gun, Nathan William Lambdin, Nancy Lorenz, Kristen Miller, Wes Mills, Jeffry Mitchell, Megan Murphy, Jenene Nagy, Ido Radon, Georgina Reskala, Joe Rudko, Tad Savinar, Susan Seubert, Adam Sorensen, Barbara Stafford, Storm Tharp, Gus Van Sant, Nell Warren, Heather Watkins, Marie Watt, and Yamamoto Masao.
events.title: Mixed Flock: 30 Years

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. In 2025, she was featured in Create! Magazine Issue #49 and is currently represented by Chefas Projects.
events.title: JESSIE WEITZEL LE GRAND | ASTRAL ACCESSORIES

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: Instructor | Tickets | Series Schedule | Parking Enjoy a blossom-filled afternoon at the beautiful Lan Su Chinese Garden with the return of Steep & Paint. With all materials provided and admission included, all you need to bring is yourself! We’re bringing this series back by popular demand and newly reimagined in partnership with the Oregon Botanical Artists \(OBA\). This immersive afternoon experience invites you to slow down, look closely, and connect with plants through tea, conversation, and hands-on art-making. Our August 14 Lotus session with Zebith Thalden will use colored pencils as the medium. Each session weaves together horticulture, tea culture, and botanical art in a relaxed, welcoming setting: Learn the plant up close: A Lan Su gardener leads a close-up botanical show-and-tell, sharing seasonal plant facts, cultural stories, and growing insights. Taste the season: Enjoy a sampling of seasonal teas from Yun Shui Teahouse. Create botanical art: An OBA artist guides a full botanical art class inspired by the featured plant. Whether you’re returning to Steep & Paint or joining for the first time, this refreshed program offers an even richer way to experience Lan Su. Bring a friend with you and let’s Steep & Paint together! Meet the Instructor: Zebith Thalden “Spice Bush or Western Sweetshrub \(Calycanthus occidentalis\)” by Zebith Thalden Zebith Thalden is a US-based studio artist, author, and instructor. Her artwork has been featured in galleries, cultural centers, and art museums, including the CICA Museum in Gimpo-si, South Korea; the Academy of Science in Canberra, Australia; American Association for the Advancement of Science in Washington DC; and the Annmarie Sculpture Garden in Dowell, Maryland. She has been in residence at Zion National Park and PLAYA: Center for the Intersection of Art and Science. She has also been a featured speaker at Portland State College of the Arts: School of Art \+ Design, Red Butte Garden and Arboretum, and Southern Utah University. Her book The Insect Artist: How to Observe, Draw, and Paint Butterflies, Bees, and More was released by Timber Press on March 12, 2024. She received an MFA from Goddard College and a BFA from the Rhode Island School of Design. Meet Our Partner: Oregon Botanical Artists \(OBA\) Oregon Botanical Artists is a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting contemporary botanical art while honoring its long-standing traditions. Founded in 2012, the organization supports a diverse community of artists who celebrate the beauty and diversity of plant life through detailed and scientifically informed artwork. Oregon Botanical Artists is affiliated with the American Society of Botanical Artists as an Artists Circle. events.summary: When an auto dealership in Longview, TX, launches an endurance contest, ten economically strapped strangers embark on a journey that tests their hearts, minds, and bodies. events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/GWDR-26 On Sale Friday, May 15 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Gillian Welch and David Rawlings are pillars of the modern acoustic music world and their rich and remarkable careers span over twenty-five years. They have been hailed by Pitchfork as “modern masters of American folk” and “protectors of the American folk song” by Rolling Stone and the New York Times says “their combined voices operate beyond simple sonic harmony. There are emotional inquiries at play. If Welch’s voice delivers the good news or the hard news of the world, Rawlings’s voice comes underneath, asking how much deeper the sadness can go or what fresh heights the ecstatic can climb to.” Their most recent 10th studio album, Woodland, won the 2025 Best Folk Album GRAMMY. Woodland was named for and recorded at Welch and Rawlings’ own Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville, TN. Of the album and studio, Welch said, “Woodland is at the heart of everything we do and has been for the last twenty some years. The past four years were spent almost entirely within its walls, bringing it back to life after the 2020 tornado and making this record. The music is \(songs are\) a swirl of contradictions, emptiness, fullness, joy, grief, destruction, permanence. Now.” The new 10-song collection mingles full band tracks with intricate duet performances all tied together with the duo’s signature sound and lyricism and cements the pair’s iconoclastic position at the forefront of acoustic music. After moving to Nashville in the 1990s, Welch was launched into the public consciousness when Emmylou Harris recorded a cover of Welch’s “Orphan Girl.” Her career continued to flourish as her 1996 debut Revival, produced by T Bone Burnett, was released to critical acclaim. Firmly on the roots music map following the release, Welch and Rawlings followed up that GRAMMY nominated album release with 1998’s Hell Among The Yearlings, a stark duet record that further solidified the duo as a force in the folk music scene

events.summary: Medical experts play a crucial role in evaluating injuries that occur during assisted childbirth by carefully reviewing medical records, delivery notes, imaging scans, and the condition of both the mother and baby. They assess whether forceps, vacuum extraction, or other assisted delivery methods were used appropriately according to accepted medical standards. Specialists also examine the timing of interventions, fetal monitoring records, and whether alternative delivery options should have been considered. Their findings help determine if the injuries resulted from unavoidable complications or preventable medical negligence. In cases involving Traume from Instrumental Delivery, experts evaluate the extent of physical and neurological harm, the expected long-term impact, and the treatment or rehabilitation that may be required. They may consult with obstetricians, pediatric neurologists, radiologists, and rehabilitation professionals to provide an objective medical opinion. This expert evidence is often essential in establishing whether the standard of care fell below what would reasonably be expected. A detailed medical assessment can also help quantify the financial and personal impact of the injury, including ongoing healthcare needs and loss of quality of life. Families seeking answers often rely on experienced legal professionals to interpret these findings within the context of a compensation claim. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases, including those involving assisted childbirth injuries, and works closely with independent medical experts to build well-supported claims. By combining detailed medical evidence with legal expertise, the firm helps clients understand their rights and pursue fair compensation where negligence has contributed to avoidable birth injuries.
events.title: How do medical experts assess injuries caused by assisted childbirth?

events.summary: Surgery always carries some level of risk, and not every unexpected outcome is the result of negligence. However, when a healthcare professional fails to meet the accepted standard of medical care and that failure causes avoidable harm, the situation may amount to Surgical Negligence. Determining the difference often requires a careful review of medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the procedure. Warning signs can include operating on the wrong site, delayed treatment of complications, retained surgical instruments, anesthesia errors, or inadequate post-operative care. It is also important to consider whether the patient was properly informed of the risks before consenting to surgery. Establishing negligence involves proving that the injury was preventable and directly caused by substandard care rather than an unavoidable complication. Because these cases can be medically and legally complex, professional legal guidance is essential. Ciano Carroll Solicitors represents individuals who believe they have suffered avoidable harm due to medical errors and helps them understand whether they may have a valid claim. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters enables clients to navigate the legal process with confidence. By working with independent medical experts and thoroughly investigating each case, the firm evaluates whether the required legal standard for negligence has been met. Anyone concerned about the outcome of a surgical procedure should seek advice as early as possible to protect their legal rights. Understanding the distinction between an accepted surgical risk and Surgical Negligence is the first step toward determining whether compensation may be available.
events.title: How can you tell if a surgical complication was actually negligence?

events.summary: Instrumental delivery can be a necessary medical intervention during childbirth, but when forceps or a vacuum extractor are used incorrectly, mothers may suffer serious physical and emotional harm. Injuries such as severe perineal tears, pelvic floor damage, nerve injuries, excessive bleeding, or long-term pain can have lasting effects on daily life. If these injuries resulted from avoidable medical errors or substandard care, the affected mother may have grounds to pursue a compensation claim. Establishing negligence typically requires evidence that healthcare professionals failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that this directly caused the injury. Every case is unique, so medical records, expert opinions, and the circumstances surrounding the delivery are carefully evaluated. Claims can help recover compensation for medical expenses, rehabilitation, lost income, ongoing care, and pain and suffering. The physical and emotional Traume from Instrumental Delivery may also be considered when assessing the full impact of the injury on the mother's quality of life. Understanding your legal rights is an important first step toward seeking justice. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance to individuals who believe their injuries were caused by negligent medical treatment. Their experience in investigating childbirth-related negligence helps clients understand whether they have a valid claim and what legal options may be available. Seeking legal advice promptly can also help preserve important evidence and ensure claims are brought within the applicable time limits.
events.title: Maternal injuries during instrumental delivery lead to compensation claims?

events.summary: When parents suspect that a birth injury could have been prevented, taking prompt and informed action is essential. The first step is to seek appropriate medical care for the child and ensure that all ongoing health concerns are properly documented. Parents should also request copies of medical records, including labour, delivery, and neonatal care notes, as these documents may help clarify what happened during childbirth. It is often beneficial to keep a detailed record of symptoms, treatments, and conversations with healthcare providers. In some situations, concerns may arise about Traume from Instrumental Delivery, particularly if forceps or a vacuum extractor were used during a difficult birth and the child later developed injuries. While not every complication is the result of negligence, a thorough legal review can determine whether accepted medical standards were followed. Understanding the cause of a birth injury can help families make informed decisions about their next steps. Experienced legal professionals can explain the claims process, the evidence required, and the applicable time limits without creating unnecessary stress for parents. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on medical negligence cases, including birth injury claims, and provides guidance to families seeking answers after a traumatic delivery. Their experience in handling complex medical negligence matters can help parents understand whether avoidable errors may have contributed to their child's injuries. Taking early action also helps preserve important evidence and protects a family's legal rights. Most importantly, parents should remember that seeking legal advice is not only about pursuing compensation but also about obtaining accountability and securing support for their child's future care and long-term needs.
events.title: What should parents do if they suspect birth trauma was avoidable?

events.summary: Proving a Surgical Negligence claim requires strong, well-documented evidence that demonstrates how a healthcare provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and caused avoidable harm. Medical records are often the foundation of the case, providing a detailed timeline of diagnosis, treatment, surgery, and follow-up care. Expert medical opinions are equally important because they help establish whether the surgeon's actions fell below the standard expected of a reasonably competent professional. Diagnostic scans, laboratory results, surgical notes, consent forms, and hospital records can further support the claim. Witness statements from medical professionals or others involved in the patient's care may also strengthen the evidence. It is essential to show not only that an error occurred but also that the mistake directly resulted in physical, emotional, or financial damage. Documentation of ongoing treatment, rehabilitation, lost income, and future medical needs can help demonstrate the full impact of the injury. Every case is unique, making a thorough investigation critical before legal proceedings begin. An experienced solicitor can identify the evidence needed, obtain independent expert reports, and build a compelling legal argument. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on complex medical negligence cases and understands the detailed approach required to investigate Surgical Negligence claims. Their experience in reviewing medical evidence and working with independent experts helps clients present well-supported claims. By carefully gathering relevant documentation and establishing causation, they aim to protect the rights of individuals affected by avoidable surgical errors. Seeking legal guidance early can also help preserve important evidence and ensure procedural deadlines are met. A well-prepared case supported by credible evidence significantly improves the likelihood of achieving a fair outcome.
events.title: What evidence is required to prove a surgical negligence claim?

events.summary: Surgical negligence under Irish law occurs when a surgeon, hospital, or other healthcare professional fails to provide the standard of care that a reasonably competent medical practitioner would have delivered in similar circumstances, resulting in avoidable harm to a patient. This can include operating on the wrong site, causing preventable surgical injuries, failing to obtain informed consent, leaving surgical instruments inside the body, or providing inadequate post-operative care. Every case is assessed on its own facts, and proving Surgical Negligence generally requires evidence showing that the accepted standard of medical care was breached and that the breach directly caused the injury. Patients may experience additional medical treatment, prolonged recovery, financial losses, or long-term physical and emotional effects because of negligent surgical care. Irish law allows eligible patients to seek compensation where negligence can be established through appropriate medical and legal evidence. Understanding your legal rights early can make a significant difference in protecting your interests and preserving important evidence. Seeking advice from experienced legal professionals helps clarify whether the circumstances meet the legal threshold for Surgical Negligence. Ciano Carroll Solicitors focuses on representing clients in complex medical negligence claims and provides guidance throughout the legal process with a clear understanding of Irish medical negligence law. Their experience in handling surgical negligence cases helps clients understand the evidence required, the claims process, and the potential outcomes. Whether the issue involves a surgical error, delayed treatment after surgery, or another avoidable complication, obtaining informed legal advice is an important first step toward pursuing justice and fair compensation.
events.title: What is considered surgical negligence under Irish law?

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present our summer group show Mixed Flock: 30 Years, marking the celebration of the gallery’s thirtieth anniversary. Mixed Flock comes from the idea of different species of birds gathering together for a variety of reasons including safety, cooperation, and community. In talking with wildlife scientist Derek Craighead about mixed flocks, Craighead suggested humans underestimate the sociability of animals, that wild animals will gather to be social, for fun, and for company. That’s worthwhile! For thirty years, PDX artist’s have been a wonderful mixed flock with each artist having their own way of seeing the world and approaching their art-making. Now is an important time to highlight and strengthen mixed flocks. Our country is a mixed flock, the “melting pot”, where diverse peoples, cultures, and ways exist together and we are better for it. This show is a celebration of the gallery’s many and varied artists, supporters, and collectors who make up our flock. Mixed Flock: 30 Years features work from represented and invited artists including: Anna Gray + Ryan Wilson Pauslen, Nick Blosser, Iván Carmona, Marjorie Dial, Amjad Faur, Bean Finneran, Jacques Flechemueller, Ellen George, Johannes GiararVictoria Haven, Elizabeth Knight, Justin L’Amie, Alma Allen, James Lavadour, Terran Last Gun, Nathan William Lambdin, Nancy Lorenz, Kristen Miller, Wes Mills, Jeffry Mitchell, Megan Murphy, Jenene Nagy, Ido Radon, Georgina Reskala, Joe Rudko, Tad Savinar, Susan Seubert, Adam Sorensen, Barbara Stafford, Storm Tharp, Gus Van Sant, Nell Warren, Heather Watkins, Marie Watt, and Yamamoto Masao.

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, San Francisco–based artist Lindsay Stripling's debut solo exhibition with the gallery. Through luminous watercolor paintings, Stripling creates dreamlike worlds where memory, intuition, and the rhythms of the natural world converge. Her imagined landscapes and nature-infused portraits blur the boundaries between observation and imagination, inviting viewers into spaces where storytelling becomes a means of navigating identity, belonging, and transformation. Rooted in experimentation, texture, and play, Stripling's practice embraces watercolor as both a precise and unpredictable medium. Layers of transparent color accumulate into richly atmospheric compositions that evoke fleeting memories, quiet psychological states, and the mysterious logic of dreams. Plants, animals, and human figures coexist in environments that feel at once deeply familiar and gently surreal, suggesting a world in which the human experience is inseparable from the more-than-human landscape. Throughout Where Do Geese Fly at Night?, Stripling explores themes of nature, time, community, psychology, and personal mythology. Rather than offering fixed narratives, her paintings unfold as open-ended visual poems, encouraging viewers to project their own memories and emotional landscapes into the work. Each composition balances meticulous craftsmanship with a spirit of curiosity, revealing beauty in uncertainty and wonder in the everyday. The exhibition's title poses a deceptively simple question, one that gestures toward the unseen journeys taking place beyond the limits of perception. Like migratory paths traced through darkness, Stripling's paintings invite contemplation of the invisible forces that shape our relationships with ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Lindsay Stripling is a San Francisco–based painter, illustrator, and educator. Working primarily in watercolor, she explores the intersections of storytelling, memory, dreams, and ecology through richly layered paintings that combine intimate portraiture with expansive natural imagery. Where Do Geese Fly at Night? marks her first solo exhibition with Chefas Projects.
events.title: LINDSAY STRIPLING | WHERE DO GEESE FLY AT NIGHT?

events.summary: Chefas Projects is delighted to welcome back sculptor Jessie Weitzel Le Grand for her fourth exhibition with the gallery entitled Astral Accessories. Communication arrives fractured: as static, interference, intuition, and half-remembered technologies that once promised connection. In Astral Accessories, Portland-based artist Jessie Weitzel Le Grand presents a new body of sculptural work that imagines obsolete technological devices as enigmatic relics from alternate realities. Equal parts artifact, machine, and living organism, the sculptures transform familiar forms into mysterious conduits for uncertainty, speculation, and wonder. Drawing on the visual language of outdated communications technology, the exhibition considers what remains when systems of transmission fail or become obsolete. Unmanageable and invisible, signals continue to pass through space, whirring beyond perception, like sirens too quiet to hear. Meaning emerges imperfectly through noise, distortion, and interruption, where messages are received as static, interference, and fragmented memory rather than clear transmission. Rather than offering resolution, Astral Accessories embraces ambiguity. The works suggest speculative tools for communicating across impossible distances: between worlds, across time, or with forms of intelligence that remain just beyond comprehension. Suspended between archaeology and science fiction, the sculptures ask viewers to reconsider the objects that mediate our relationships with technology, memory, and the unknown. Utilizing an eclectic array of materials, including ceramics, thermoplastic, flashe paint, and even materials used in fly tying, Weitzel Le Grand blurs the boundaries between art, artifact, and technology. Interested in exploring how we perceive reality and questioning the certainty of what we see, she embeds natural elements such as orchids, moths, and fragments of coral within computer motherboards, rotary telephones, and other obsolete technologies in disorienting, exuberant configurations. By reimagining these nostalgic devices in playful yet unfamiliar ways, she encourages viewers to question their function and invent their own narratives around the mysterious systems they seem to inhabit. By transforming obsolete technologies into uncanny relics, Weitzel Le Grand creates a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and failed technologies become vessels for new forms of connection. Jessie Weitzel Le Grand (b. 1987) was born and raised in Portland, Oregon, where she continues to live and work. She received a BFA from the Pacific Northwest College of Art and an MAT from Marylhurst University. Her work has recently been exhibited at Galerie Lefebvre & Fils (Paris, France), Outback Arthouse (Los Angeles, California), Oregon Contemporary (Portland, Oregon), and as part of Lazy Oaf's Take A Break exhibition (London, United Kingdom). She is the co-founder of carnation Contemporary, a collective of emerging and mid-career artists from the Pacific Northwest championing critical contemporary art, and Well Well Projects, an artist-member gallery in Portland's Kenton neighborhood. In 2025, she was featured in Create! Magazine Issue #49 and is currently represented by Chefas Projects.
events.title: JESSIE WEITZEL LE GRAND | ASTRAL ACCESSORIES

events.summary: Founded in 2025 by award-winning classical guitar virtuoso and Artistic Director, Tye Austin, M.M., Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness is a fiscally sponsored nonprofit concert series presenting open-air classical guitar concerts staged in the wilderness of the Pacific Northwest. From August 1 through October 1, Oregon native Tye Austin will perform more than 30 intimate outdoor concerts across 15 of Oregon's most breathtaking state parks—from coastal bluffs to old-growth forests, red rock canyons, thundering waterfalls, vineyards, and ranches. Audiences will experience world-class live music performances through our signature Wilder Sound wireless headphone technology, allowing every guest to enjoy crystal-clear audio while remaining immersed in the beauty of the natural world up to a 1/4 mile radius from the stage. Wilder Frets is more than a concert series. It is a community movement dedicated to making exceptional live music concerts and masterclasses accessible to everyone. Every ticket purchased helps support our growing community initiatives, including: Fret Not Tickets Program, providing complimentary concert tickets to individuals and families facing financial barriers. The Free Frets Initiative, donating free classical guitars, free masterclasses, and mentorship to at-risk from rural, tribal, and urban communities throughout Oregon. Our inaugural season has been made possible through the generosity of our season sponsors and community partners such as Heartbeat Silent Disco, Community Beats, Willamette Valley Music Company, the Maslow Project, and Oregon State Parks who believe that arts, education, conservation, and public access belong together. Whether you're an experienced concertgoer, an outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a meaningful way to spend an evening, Wilder Frets offers an unforgettable experience unlike anything else in the Pacific Northwest. Join us this season and discover why music sounds even more extraordinary in the great outdoors. View complete tour schedule and purchase tickets online only at www.wilderfrets.org/tour
events.title: Wilder Frets: Classical Guitar in the Wilderness - Inaugural Concert Season

events.summary: Join Argentine classical guitarist Luciano Marazzo for an intimate evening of music celebrating the rich traditions of Latin American and Spanish guitar. events.summary: TICKETS truewest.info/GWDR26 On Sale Friday, May 1 at 10am PT This Event is All Ages ---------------------------------------- Gillian Welch and David Rawlings are pillars of the modern acoustic music world and their rich and remarkable careers span over twenty-five years. They have been hailed by Pitchfork as “modern masters of American folk” and “protectors of the American folk song” by Rolling Stone and the New York Times says “their combined voices operate beyond simple sonic harmony. There are emotional inquiries at play. If Welch’s voice delivers the good news or the hard news of the world, Rawlings’s voice comes underneath, asking how much deeper the sadness can go or what fresh heights the ecstatic can climb to.” Their most recent 10th studio album, Woodland, won the 2025 Best Folk Album GRAMMY. Woodland was named for and recorded at Welch and Rawlings’ own Woodland Sound Studios in Nashville, TN. Of the album and studio, Welch said, “Woodland is at the heart of everything we do and has been for the last twenty some years. The past four years were spent almost entirely within its walls, bringing it back to life after the 2020 tornado and making this record. The music is \(songs are\) a swirl of contradictions, emptiness, fullness, joy, grief, destruction, permanence. Now.” The new 10-song collection mingles full band tracks with intricate duet performances all tied together with the duo’s signature sound and lyricism and cements the pair’s iconoclastic position at the forefront of acoustic music. After moving to Nashville in the 1990s, Welch was launched into the public consciousness when Emmylou Harris recorded a cover of Welch’s “Orphan Girl.” Her career continued to flourish as her 1996 debut Revival, produced by T Bone Burnett, was released to critical acclaim. Firmly on the roots music map following the release, Welch and Rawlings followed up that GRAMMY nominated album release with 1998’s Hell Among The Yearlings, a stark duet record that further solidified the duo as a force in the folk music scene
